messages:
morgan: RFC up — 'Cost surface and acceptance criteria for Optimize Toolkit (batching / caching / quantization)'. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1955554321
morgan: TL;DR: need concrete launch gates (SLOs, regression budget, perf delta thresholds) + short runbook for rollouts. Asking infra/runtime/product for acceptance criteria and edge cases.
julie: skimmed, looks good. can we add customer-driven thresholds? e.g., p95 latency increase <= 20% for tier-1 customers when applying quantization.
kevin: +1. Also propose an automatic fallback: if eval-quality drops >2% on a tuned prompt set, disable quant variant and route to full-precision.
rishi: important: caching changes can cause cross-tenant hits if keying isn't scoped. add explicit requirement: KV keys include tenant_id + request_fingerprint and are encrypted at rest.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: rfc-drafts/1955554321 -> staging on Wed 03:00 UTC (CI checks pending) :gear:
emily: edge-case: micro prompts (<16 tokens) + batching = batching overhead hurts tail latency. Acceptance should include a small-batch latency SLO and a strategy to bypass batching for sub-16 token requests.
dave: on metrics — we should track: tokens/sec/GPU, cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency, p99 latency, and eval-quality (task-specific). For each, define min acceptable and target.
morgan: thanks. can folks paste proposed numeric thresholds here? I'll consolidate and update the doc by EOD.
julie: suggested thresholds: p95 < 120ms for short chat (seq<=64), p95 < 400ms for long form (seq<=2048), cost reduction >= 15% from quant+batching, eval-quality loss <= 1% absolute on customer eval sets.
kevin: add to rollout runbook: if p95 regresses >20% after rollout, rollback immediately and open a P1 incident. include automated alert.
morgan: noted. I'll add runbook + test datasets + gating CI. tagging @rishi @emily @dave for final signoff.
kevin: looks good to me. :thumbsup:
morgan: thanks — merging in 2h unless objections.
